issues.what: After only two searches, both keyed on the same "Sky News" + "Trump declares victory" banner, the worker reports INCOMPLETE: "the original source was not found in two searches". No image-only reverse search was run on any frame (E3/E8/E10), there was no search for "ROAD TO 270 WHAT IF" (named in the turn-1 rationale), and no exact-phrase search used distinctive transcript lines from E11 (e.g. "four electoral college votes away", "Maine's second electoral district is one").
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches the student to give up on provenance after two near-duplicate text searches, so it will under-recall originals and produce the negative reports the verifier rejects.
issues.ideal: Before declaring the original not found, run an image→video reverse search on one or two frames plus an exact-quote search from the ASR transcript (and the "ROAD TO 270" graphic text).

issues.what: Rule G3_finish_unfixable_gap FINISHes right after a single INCOMPLETE report whose stated gap is only "not found in two searches". That gap is fixable with more search angles, yet no round-2 task was assigned.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches the coordinator to treat a thin search effort as an unfixable gap and finish with the must-answer point (original + diff times) still open.
issues.ideal: Dispatch a round-2 task whose Scope is a reverse image search on E3/E8 frames and quote searches from E11, then compare_media against any candidate.

issues.what: The second query, "Sky News 2024 Wisconsin \"too close to call\" \"Trump declares victory\"", has the same intent as the first (Sky News + banner) and adds only generic results-board words. The first search had already returned off-target titles (e.g. "Trump's Nevada lawsuit", "Trump is already 'planning for 2024'") with 0% content match.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: Reformulating with the same generic broadcast banner teaches low-diversity search instead of switching cue type after a miss.
issues.ideal: Switch cue type: use a transcript quote or an image-only reverse search instead of another banner-keyword variant.

issues.what: The report builds its findings on the single frame E5. F2 is filler ("The cited frame documents Material A at 31.44 s, with a recorded presentation interval of 31.44–31.48 s"), and the limitation says intervals "0.04–31.44 s, 31.48–78.6 s ... remain visually unconfirmed" even though frames E3/E8/E10 were in focus. The ASR transcript E11 (Alaska / 270 / Maine discussion) is never reported or cited.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches thin reports that drop evidence already gathered (other frames, transcript) and pad with a content-free finding.
issues.ideal: Report what was established (the content of E3/E8/E10 and the E11 speech with times, citing E11), drop F2, and keep the honest INCOMPLETE status for the missing original.

issues.what: The answer attaches [E5] to negative statements that E5 cannot support: "No original source video was established, so the source remains undetermined ... [E5]" and "removals, additions, reordering ... remain unverified ... [E5]".
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches citing a frame as decoration on statements about search outcomes that the frame says nothing about.
issues.ideal: Cite E5 only for the frame description; state the search/comparison gap without a citation, or cite the search records.

issues.what: T1 copies the overall task text verbatim ("The given video circulated online. Find its original source video ...") with no hint of which search cues to use.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: Copying the task verbatim teaches no decomposition, though a single-chain A-family task can reasonably go to one workspace.
issues.ideal: Keep one workspace, but phrase T1 with its sub-steps (search with frame/transcript cues, reverse image search, compare_media on the candidate, report removed intervals in both timelines).

good_patterns: ASR is run on the material before searching, and the rationale explains why (searchable wording plus later audio correspondence checks).
Query terms come from visible cues (frame banner, the Wisconsin board on E5, and transcript topics) and not from hidden knowledge; no leaked names or dates beyond what the frames and E11 show.
Honest negative: Sky News branding is explicitly not treated as proof of original publication, and the limitations admit that some candidates were not compared.
Status INCOMPLETE with a specific reason fits the actual absence of an established original; nothing is overclaimed about edits.
cannot_judge: The observation of the second (text_image) search in request_0005 is not rendered, so I cannot tell whether any candidate (E23–E38 in the next state) had a nonzero content match that should have been compared.
The first search showed 10 more results that are not rendered; one of them may have matched.
The values "Trump 50.9% and Harris 47.5%", "2024" and "ROAD TO 270 WHAT IF" come from frame images, which I cannot see in this rendering.
34 of the 45 ASR segments are truncated, so I cannot check for better quote-search candidates or for speech the report should have described.
summary: The A-family run gathered good cues (frame banners, ASR) and stayed honest about not finding the original, but it gave up after two near-identical banner-keyword searches. It never tried an image-only reverse search or a transcript-quote search, and GIA then finished immediately under an 'unfixable gap' rule. The report is thin: it rests on one frame, includes a filler finding, and leaves the transcript uncited. The rejection by the verifier looks justified mainly by the premature termination, not by any false statement in the report.
